en: Mount Mayon in Albay is globally famous for possessing one of the most perfectly symmetrical volcanic cone shapes on Earth.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park features an eight-kilometer underground river that flows directly through a cave into the sea.
The 1,268 symmetrical mounds of Bohol's Chocolate Hills are actually uplifted coral formations shaped by thousands of years of water erosion.
The Verde Island Passage, located between Batangas and Mindoro, contains the highest concentration of marine shorefish biodiversity anywhere on Earth.
Mount Hamiguitan Range Wildlife Sanctuary in Davao Oriental features a unique pygmy forest where century-old trees grow only a few feet tall.
The Marikina Valley Fault System is a 100-kilometer-long fracture zone that runs directly through the highly populated Metro Manila area.
Mount Pulag's famous sea of clouds occurs because its 2,928-meter peak reaches above the condensation level of surrounding moist air.
The Agusan Marsh Wildlife Sanctuary in Mindanao is the largest freshwater swamp forest in the Philippines and serves as a massive natural sponge.
Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park is a UNESCO World Heritage site located entirely in the middle of the Sulu Sea, far from any land.
The main chamber of Callao Cave in Peñablanca is so massive that it naturally forms a cathedral-like space large enough to hold a basketball court.
The Philippines is a top global producer of nickel, primarily mined from the iron-rich laterite soils of the Surigao peninsula.
Taal Lake in Batangas is the third-largest lake in the Philippines and was formed by massive prehistoric volcanic eruptions that created a giant caldera.
